analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow in VM is caused by malformed irep layout produced by compiler. In scope_finish(), irep->iseq is reallocated with size `sizeof(mrb_code)*s->pc + catchsize` (catch handlers appended after bytecode), but irep->ilen is set to `s->pc` (instruction count) without accounting for extra trailing catch bytes sharing the same allocation. Later VM execution (mrb_vm_exec in mruby/src/vm.c, OP_LOADL at line ~1138) reads operands from bytecode/pool using corrupted/truncated instruction stream metadata, leading to out-of-bounds pool index read (`pool[b]`) and 1-byte heap OOB read.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: mruby_fuzzer passes attacker-controlled bytes as Ruby source to mrb_load_string(). For this PoV (`\xff=91327;9`), parser/codegen emits an irep where final bytecode/catch-table packing from scope_finish results in inconsistent irep metadata used by VM. During mrb_top_run -> mrb_vm_run -> mrb_vm_exec, an OP_LOADL instruction is executed with invalid operand `b` (pool index) and VM reads past the 10-byte pool allocation. Trigger requires compiling crafted source through mruby compiler path (not just VM on trusted irep).
